questions.q: Why does sys.databases show every database on the instance, while sys.tables only shows tables in the current database?
options: sys.databases requires sysadmin permissions that sys.tables does not
sys.tables is deprecated and only works in older SQL Server versions
sys.databases is instance-wide metadata; sys.tables, sys.columns, and sys.indexes are scoped to whichever database you're connected to
There is no real difference — both return the same rows
questions.explain: sys.databases reflects the whole instance; sys.tables, sys.columns, and sys.indexes are database-scoped catalog views.

questions.q: What column in sys.databases tells you whether a database is ONLINE, RESTORING, or SUSPECT?
questions.explain: state_desc reports the database's current state — a key first check when an app can't connect.

questions.q: What key do you join sys.tables and sys.columns on to list every column in a table?
questions.explain: Every object in a database has an object_id, which sys.columns references to identify which table each column belongs to.

questions.q: Which catalog view lists the indexes (and heap, if present) defined on a table?
questions.explain: sys.indexes returns one row per index (plus a HEAP row if the table has no clustered index) for a given object_id.

questions.q: What is a catalog view, in SQL Server terms?
options: A deprecated feature replaced entirely by Dynamic Management Views
A temporary view that exists only for the life of a session
A built-in system view that exposes SQL Server metadata as regular, queryable rows
A user-created view that summarizes business data for reporting
questions.explain: Catalog views are built-in views over SQL Server's internal metadata tables, queried with ordinary SELECT statements.
